evidence: Flat directory structure with clear modules (database/, plugins/, root-level utilities) — characteristic of a modular monolith
No packages defined (packages: 0) but logical grouping via directories suggests internal modularity without formal packaging
Single entry point (bot.py) coordinating all functionality via imports from modules
Plugins depend directly on database modules and shared utilities (utils.py, info.py), indicating tight cohesion within modules but low inter-module decoupling — typical of modular monoliths
All components run in a single process (bot.py instantiates one Pyrogram Client); no inter-process or network boundaries
risks: High coupling between plugins and database layers limits testability and maintainability
No explicit dependency boundaries increase risk of circular dependencies as the project scales
Single point of failure — failure in one module can cascade across the entire application
Lack of packaging (packages: 0) suggests limited modularity in build/deployment, reducing flexibility for future decomposition
